name: maybe_Ui_EquipmentDetail_ScrollNameA
summary: One direction of the equipment detail's member-name scroll: when the member's name cursor (+0x14) is 0 it opens the wrapped detail page (page states 3 and 0x30), otherwise it measures the member's name, adds the width to the cursor (page states 1/2) and pushes the item's detail page; at the very end of the name it closes the detail again (states 3/4).
evidence: The named neighbours (Ui_Window_PushPane, Ui_Panel_ResetAndPush, Item_LookupRecord through the N_027 equipment-window helpers) keep it inside the equipment detail, but nothing in the body or in vtable 0x76A2D8 says which input direction reaches this slot, so the A/B suffix has to stay.

name: maybe_Ui_EquipmentDetail_ScrollNameB
summary: Second direction of the same name scroll: clamps the member cursor at +0x16 into [0, +0x12], sends the consumed delta as page command 10, and additionally pushes command 0x32 when the current item id is equipment (0xA4..0x9BF / 0xB19..0xB1C).
evidence: Same named callee set as 0x3D6480 plus the equipment id-range test (0xA4/0xB19) from the established facts, which proves an equipment window but still not which direction (left/right) this vtable slot 0x76A358 +2 handles.

name: Ui_DispatchCallback
summary: Runs the callback of the table's current (top) entry: entry = self[count*3+1], flags = self[count*3+2]; bit 0 of the flags marks the stored pointer as a vtable offset, so the real target is fetched through the object vtable before the call. Returns 1 when an entry existed.
evidence: All five named callers are UI window helpers (Ui_EquipmentWindow_OpenDetail, Ui_EquipmentWindow_PlayAnim, Ui_Panel_ResetAndPush), i.e. code that has just pushed a page and needs 'run the pending UI callback'; the body only invokes, so the generic name is what the evidence supports.

name: maybe_Ui_Panel_OpenDetailForCurrentId
summary: Epilogue shared by the equipment detail handlers: performs the common UI refresh, asks the panel for its current 16-bit item id, and either pushes the panel's detail page (storing the sub-panel at owner+0x10CC) or tears the panel down when the id is 0.
evidence: 'HandleCommand' was too broad: the body is byte-for-byte the epilogue of 0x3D6480/0x3D6750 (same owner+0x10CC store followed by Ui_Panel_ResetAndPush, or the close helper 0x19AD70), so it is the 'open the detail page for the current id' step. Ghidra lost the receiver (unaff_r4), so the name stays maybe_.

name: Ui_DiveForm_OnCursorInput
signature: void Ui_DiveForm_OnCursorInput(UiDiveForm* self, u32 arg2, u32 b, u32 c)
summary: Cursor-input handler of the dive form's two-tab selection list at +0xDB8: masks the event word (+0x3770) for cancel/left-right/confirm bits, forwards to the two-tab cursor and icon-type setters, and pushes or pops the form's pane depending on the resulting cursor.
evidence: The callees are now named Ui_CursorIcon_SetWordType, Ui_DiveForm_PushPane and Ui_DiveForm_PopPane, and the event bits (4, 0x142, 0x10, 1) are exactly the cancel/direction/confirm mask of the shared two-tab cursor, so the function is the form's input callback.

name: Ui_SlotTable_Refresh
signature: void Ui_SlotTable_Refresh(void* self, void* speaker, const void* record)
summary: Refreshes the talk slot table from the current speaker record: clears the two presence flags, compares the stored view position with the ten slot entries and re-applies or re-rolls the matching slot through the named slot-table helpers.
evidence: Sole named caller Field_SetupTalkParams plus the now-named callees Ui_SlotTable_RollRandomEntries / GetSelectedId / SelectEntry / ApplyEntry make the refresh role explicit; the old name and this context agree.

name: Battle_SetupUnitModelParts
signature: void Battle_SetupUnitModelParts(BattleUnit* self, u16 modelId, u8 variant)
summary: Initialises a battle unit's model from its data record: copies model id, palette, part list and part bytes out of the 0x63F1E0 record, resolves the default variant through the game work and registers the parts via Model_SetupPartsFromTable (0x2AB37C).
evidence: The callee is now named Battle_Unit_ApplyModelParts (0x2AB37C) and the callers include LoadBattleFunc (0x1471B0) and the battle unit constructors at 0x591B08/0x59A8A4, which is exactly the 'fill the unit's model parts from the monster record' role.

name: maybe_Battle_Unit_SetPresentFlag
summary: Sets the unit record's present byte (+0x10) to 1, then clears it again when the game work's actor class test 0x66AAB4 reports the special/guest actor class.
evidence: The deciding helper 0x66AAB4 is still unnamed, so whether the byte means 'visible' or 'participates in this battle' cannot be settled; the two named callers (Battle_InitializeUnitDisplay, Battle_Unit_ApplyModelParts) only place it in battle-unit setup.

name: Field_SceneObject_CreateRenderObject
summary: Creates the drawable for a field scene object: resolves the sprite/appearance descriptor from the object definition (+0x298), builds the draw object via Field_SceneObject_CreateDrawObject with a randomised parameter record, then applies the definition's mesh or animation.
evidence: Caller Field_SceneObject_InitFromDef and callees Field_SceneObject_CreateDrawObject / Field_SceneInit_AllocateAlignedBlocks are named and describe the whole chain; the body stores the result into the object's f_29C draw slot.

name: Gfx_Effect2D_EndFrame
summary: Closes the per-frame 2D-effect pass of the UI core (0x239A1C on uiCore+0x48); the matching open call is 0x3E49CC.
evidence: 0x3E49CC is now maybe_Gfx_Effect2D_BeginFrame (same 32-byte wrapper shape, same UI-core pointer), and the callers are actor-action end routines plus Ui_Effect2DOverlay_End, so the begin/end bracket reading is supported by both halves.

name: maybe_Field_Actor_UpdateMotionPose
summary: Re-applies the actor's procedural motion pose: selects the row of the 0x39-entry, 0x30-byte motion table from the body type (+0x200) and the animation progress (+0x1FC), interpolates between two rows and writes the model size, animation id, walk speeds, gravity and collision values.
evidence: 'LoadMotionSet' described the wrong lifetime: the named callers Field_Actor_Suspend, maybe_Field_Actor_DeleteFromScene and maybe_Model_Actor_UpdateScale call it to re-apply the current pose/size before changing state, and the body samples the table by frame progress (float interpolation) on every call.

name: maybe_Ui_Casino_SetPrizeCounterText
summary: Formats a counter from the bag block (work+0x24A98, the block whose +0x28 is gold) into message slot 0x00640025 and applies the resulting string to pane 0x21 of the prize window.
evidence: 'DebugLabel' was wrong: both callers are casino prize windows (Ui_PokerWindow_Payout, Ui_CasinoPrizeWindow_Ctor), the value comes from the shared money formatter 0x66B2CC on the bag, and the result goes into a normal message pane (0x1A6680/0x633560) - the prize counter, not a debug label.

name: Pack_AcquireResourceHandle18
signature: int Pack_AcquireResourceHandle18(PackHandle* out, PackEntry* entry, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Handle-acquire variant of Pack_AcquireResourceHandle (0x6F0F5C) that additionally requires the resolved part to be exactly 0x18 bytes, using its own handle table (0x6F2D90/D94/D9C).
evidence: Its sibling 0x6F0F5C is now the confident Pack_AcquireResourceHandle, the callees Pack_FreeHandleEntry/Pack_ReleaseHandle are named, and the callers (Ui_MedalPrizeWindow_Ctor, Ui_CasinoPrizeWindow_Ctor) are the two windows that load this fixed-size format.

name: maybe_Field_Marker_CreateVisual
summary: Builds the visual object of a map marker: copies the marker's default sprite block, resolves the actor's transform record (0x641F88/0x644BBC), allocates the 0x240-byte sprite object (vtable 0x76E2C0) with sprite id 0x32F, registers it with the 2D effect manager and aims it at the actor.
evidence: Only the sprite id 0x32F and the 0x240-byte class identify the visual; neither the class nor 0x32F is named anywhere, and the single caller sits in the actor-record lookup path, so which kind of marker this draws is still open.

name: Ui_SmithMenu_OpenDefaultPage
summary: After a mode change the smith menu applies the pending mode (0x3EC01C), empties the pane stack through the named Ui_SmithMenu_PopPaneDetail, pushes the default page (Ui_SmithMenu_PushPane) and runs its entry delegate.
evidence: All callees are now the named Ui_SmithMenu_* helpers and the page base comes from the smith vtable table 0x72B43C; the body is exactly 'reset to the default page after a mode switch'.

name: Os_FindObjectByHandle
summary: Resolves a 32-bit object handle through the shared handle table at 0x7BA2D0 (bucket/key validation) and returns the registered object of the expected class, or NULL.
evidence: All four callers are named monster-model routines (Monster_Model_Create, Monster_Model_CreateDualPattern, Monster_Model_SetupPattern, Monster_AttachAnimation), so the generic handle-registry lookup is used as the 'get the registered monster model for this handle' primitive; the class test is the marker 0x7C8584. The decompilation is only cosmetically damaged: the unaff_r5 register is supplied by the disassembly at 0x421170 ('addsne r5, r0, #0x7c' = the interface list head), and the bucket/key walk is intact in asm.

name: Monster_Pattern_LoadModel
summary: Loads the shared monster model pattern for an id: formats and loads 'pattern_%02d.bch', then reads the integer out of the matching 'pattern_%02d' table into +0x18.
evidence: The two format strings and Script_GetIntTable1 are unambiguous, and both callers (0x420D48, 0x422BE0) are named monster-model constructors that also load 'enemy_%s%d.ani'.

name: Field_GameObject_Ctor
summary: Constructor of the large (0x14B4-byte) field game object: chains the interactive-object base with vtable 0x76C1A0, seeds the id fields with -1/0xFFFFFC00 sentinels, builds the two chained sub-objects and resets the embedded party member slot.
evidence: The refiner's vtable siblings are named Field_ObjectFactory_GameObject / Field_ObjectFactory_Kind04 (the factories that allocate this size) and the base is Field_InteractiveObject_Ctor, so 'Field_GameObject_Ctor' is what the callers already imply.

name: Model_CreateAttachedEffect
signature: u32 Model_CreateAttachedEffect(CharacterModel* self, ItemRecord* item, const void* nodeDesc)
summary: Builds the effect node that visualises an equipped item: copies the item's 0x12-byte effect parameter block plus its colour/scale fields, creates the attached effect (0x2239F4) and binds it to the model at the descriptor's node via Model_AttachSlot_Setup.
evidence: The callee set is now named (Item_LookupRecord, Model_AttachSlot_Setup, maybe_Effect_CreateAttached2) and the caller 0x40A758 passes the item record plus the transform block, so the effect-from-item role is supported.

name: Gfx_SpriteActor_AddRotationChild
summary: Adds one child quad to a sprite actor: copies the child's six transform floats into the actor's per-child table, rotates them by the parent matrix and submits either a rotated (type 2, Gfx_Scene_AddSpriteEntryLarge) or billboard (type 1, AddSpriteEntrySmall) sprite; the handle lands in self[0x17].
evidence: Both draw helpers are named now and the branch on def+0x14 == 1/2 is the billboard/rotated distinction, exactly as the first pass read it.

name: Gfx_Trail_AddSegment
summary: Appends one segment to a 16-segment trail: stores the six floats, transforms them by the parent matrix and submits a rotated (Gfx_Scene_AddNodeType2) or billboard (AddNodeType1) quad; returns 0 when the ring is full.
evidence: The draw helpers are named and the 0x10 cap / 0x18 stride match the earlier reading; the returned 1/0 is the 'added' flag.

name: maybe_Gfx_SpriteNode_EmitBurst
summary: Builds an effect/sound descriptor in front of the camera for a sprite node and spawns it (0x35FF3C) with SE 0xFD once the node's marker becomes visible.
evidence: Ghidra still truncates the control flow here (halt_baddata, unaff_r7/r8), so the trigger condition and the exact descriptor contents remain unverified; the camera-facing burst reading is the only consistent story.

name: Field_Object2D_UpdateEffectSlot
summary: Per-frame update of a 2D field object's attached effect: runs the standard prelude, restarts the effect through 0x40D7E0 when the object is active, then pushes the object's world position into the 2D effect manager (0x6224F8).
evidence: The restart callee 0x40D7E0 is now maybe_Field_Object2D_RestartStateEffect and the neighbour 0x4E667C pushes positions to the same manager, so 'update the object's effect slot' is supported.

name: maybe_Field_Prop_UpdateChildVisibility
summary: Validates the prop's handle at +0x2CC and then calls the child node's vtable+0x18 with the config's visibility byte, so the prop's separate child visual follows the config state.
evidence: Only the single neighbour Field_HandleIsValid is named; the child at +0x4C and the config byte at +0x1C are unnamed fields, so what exactly is shown/hidden stays a guess.

name: maybe_Field_DrawObject_InitWorkData
signature: void maybe_Field_DrawObject_InitWorkData(UiWindow* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32* rect, short* size, u8 arg6, const void* data, u32 arg8, u32 arg9, u32 arg10)
summary: Initialises a freshly created draw object's work fields from a scene definition: rectangle, text origin and size, the two resource ids, the 0x84-byte parameter block and three opaque caller values, then resets the state/cursor bytes.
evidence: 'Ui_Window_InitWorkData' named the wrong class: all four callers are scene-object draw-object creators (Field_SceneObject_CreateRenderObject, Field_Gimmick3107_SetupDrawObjectFromDesc/FromTemplate, 0x3DE0B4) and the fields filled belong to the draw handle stored at f_29C, not to UI window panes.

name: Battle_ActorAction_SpawnThreeEffects
summary: Spawns the effect set of a battle actor action (three FindOrCreateInstance effects) after playing the action's SE, and initialises the action's effect state from the shared defaults table.
evidence: The effect helper is now named Effect_FindOrCreateInstance, the SE id comes from the action record (0x63FD24 + 0x63E60C), and the caller count grew to the battle action code, so 'spawn the effects of this action' is supported.

name: Battle_ActorAction_UpdateReaction
summary: State machine for a battle actor's reaction (hit/stagger) animation: looks up the action record, walks the state at +0x62B, spawns the popup entries and plays the reaction animation until the done byte at +0x1386 is set.
evidence: Its neighbours are now named (Battle_ActorAction_UpdateActionState, Battle_ActorAction_UpdateSubCommands, Battle_Ui_ForwardCommand) and the body is a dispatcher over the same per-actor state fields, so the reaction-update role holds.

name: Anim_TimeTrack_Init
signature: void Anim_TimeTrack_Init(AnimTimeTrack* self, int preset, void* heap)
summary: Initialises a timeline track from one of four presets: stores the preset's duration and scale, clears the cursor fields and inserts the first zero-length keyframe into the track's list.
evidence: The callers are now named battle-scene time-track users (BattleScene_ResetAndInitTimeTracks, BattleScene_UpdateScreenState0Main) and the insertion goes through the named keyframe-list helper, so the track-setup role is confirmed.

name: Field_SceneObject_ResetMoveTarget
summary: Clears a scene object's movement target: resets the target ids to the 0xFFFF sentinel, asks the field command system (0x256678, command 8) for the new target and stores the resolved name handle, so the object idles until a new target arrives.
evidence: Callers are now named field object/gadget updates (Field_Gadget_AddAndTriggerCommand, Field_SceneObject_PlayBreakReaction) and the 0xFFFF sentinel pattern matches the pack-resolve helper, so 'reset the move target' is supported.

name: maybe_Effect_Emitter_ReadVariant
summary: Loads one variant/state record into an object's f_298..f_2B4 block: resets the four variant fields to the 0xFFFF defaults, then fills them from the variant table entry (0x63DCE8) and marks the variant as used.
evidence: The same f_298/f_2AC/f_2B4 block is reset by the now-named Field_SceneObject_ResetMoveTarget (0x44A334), so the object is a field scene object rather than a proven effect emitter; whether the variant is an effect or a movement variant is still open.

name: maybe_Effect_ParticleEmitter_InitPoolD
summary: Fourth emitter/pool initialiser: builds a 0xAC-byte object on the alternate base initialiser 0x5F2B54 with a 64-entry two-word pool (0x100050(obj+9, 0x44EDD0, 0x40, 2)) and copies its defaults from the 0x44EDC8 table.
evidence: The base 0x5F2B54 is now Gfx_Sprite_CreateInstance, i.e. this is a sprite/particle pool constructor, but which visual family the 0x44EDCC vtable belongs to is still unidentified, so the D suffix stays.

name: maybe_Ui_OverlaySlot_CreateSpriteWithArgs
summary: Variant of the slot sprite creator that builds a 200x120 sprite mesh through Gfx_CreateSpriteMesh with the extra type-2 argument vector and stores the result in the slot's f_B8.
evidence: The two factories are named (Gfx_CreateSpriteMesh, Gfx_Sprite_CreateInstance) but the owning class (the 'overlay slot') is still inferred only from the f_B8 handle and the 0x31Axxx helper family.

name: Ui_MessagePage_DtorDelete
summary: Deleting destructor of a message page: stores the class pointer, releases its pack handle, runs the named message-page / horserace-message child destructors and frees the object.
evidence: Almost every callee is named now (Pack_ReleaseHandle, Ui_HorseraceReceptMsg_Release, Ui_MessagePage_Dtor, Ui_Object_DtorBase) and the sequence is the standard delete path, so this is the deleting destructor, not the plain one.

name: Ui_Pack_LoadLayoutChecked
summary: Checked layout-pack loader: returns 0 when the pack cannot be opened, otherwise runs the same open/'%s.pack'/Fs_NamedObject_LoadSimple chain as 0x4546A8 and reports whether the new handle was accepted into +0x828.
evidence: The sibling 0x4546A8 is now maybe_Ui_Pack_LoadLayout and the callees Fs_NamedObject_LoadSimple / Ui_LayoutAnim_Reset / Pack_ReleaseHandle are named, so the 'checked variant of the layout loader' reading holds.

name: Ui_Pack_UnloadLayout
summary: Unloads the cached UI layout pack: resets the owner (Ui_LayoutAnim_Reset), releases the handle at +0x828 and wipes the 0x12 per-entry blocks with the class fill pattern.
evidence: The named callees (Ui_LayoutAnim_Reset, Pack_ReleaseHandle, std_destroy_range) match the loader's fields exactly, and the sole caller 0x626E44 is a UI teardown path.

name: Ui_PartyStatusWindow_Update
summary: State machine of the party status window: states -1/0x9E0 rebuild the member rows, 0x9E1..0x9DF wait for the character to settle, 0x9E6/0x9E9 finish; it also raises the 0x9A 'not available' popup and polls the field-event system until it is free.
evidence: The neighbours are now named (Ui_PartyWindow_SyncMemberOrder, Ui_PopupEntry_SpawnFromTable, Actor_IsIdleAndQueueEmpty) and the state constants match a party window's row refresh, so the update role is supported.

name: Gfx_MoveNode_CreateA
signature: void Gfx_MoveNode_CreateA(u8 mode, u32 startX, u32 startY, u32 duration)
summary: Allocates a 0xA0-byte movement node from the UI pool, installs the node vtable with the update routine 0x46B4C0 and the three start values, and appends it to the active sprite-animation node map.
evidence: The named neighbour Container_NamedMap_Insert is exactly how the node is published (app+0x78) and the allocation/ctor pattern is the same as the sibling creators, so the 'create a move node' reading is supported.

name: Gfx_CreateNodeNamedShakeA
signature: void* Gfx_CreateNodeNamedShakeA(GfxNodeMap* map, u8 mode, u32 p0, u32 p1, u32 p2)
summary: Creates a node called 'Shake' in the animation node map, installs its vtable and stores the four parameters; the node drives a screen-shake style offset.
evidence: The string literal 'Shake' (0x46B5A4) plus the named callee Container_NameHash_Ctor pin the name, and the vtable/default-block pattern matches the sibling node creators.

name: Ui_TargetMarkerContainer_Dtor
summary: Base destructor of the battle target-marker/effect container: stores the vtable argument, destroys the effect sub-object, releases the marker list (Ui_BattleTargetMarker_ReleaseAll), the anim model instance and the 0x14-entry array, then restores the base vtable and walks the second list before freeing.
evidence: 'ReleaseAll' was misleading because the function *calls* the named Ui_BattleTargetMarker_ReleaseAll; the body is the container's destructor (vtable store + every owned sub-object released + operator-delete path) and it is the smaller sibling of 0x46C8C4.

name: Ui_BattleScreen_Dtor
summary: Base destructor of the battle screen object: restores the two vtables, releases the target-marker/anim sub-objects at +0xED40/+0xED48, destroys the two inline arrays (0x14 x2 and 0xE4 x 0x10) and the nested screen object.
evidence: All callees are named (Ui_BattleTargetMarker_ReleaseAll, Anim_ModelInstance_Release, maybe_Battle_Effect_Dtor, std_destroy_range) and the same vtable-store pattern as the target-marker container dtor identifies it as the class' base destructor.

name: Battle_CreateEnemyDisplay
summary: Builds the on-screen representation of a battle participant from a 0x98-byte descriptor: fills the layout record, picks the monster/party model data and registers the result with the battle UI.
evidence: The callee Battle_SetupUnitFromMonsterData (0x19F17C) is named and the callers are the battle setup routines (0x2BDAC8/0x2BE754/0x4E55AC), so the display-creation role is supported.

name: Battle_Message_ResolveRowOffset
summary: Returns the vertical offset of a battle-message row: combines the row flag word with the message object's height (+0xF38) and row base (+0xB78), and returns the icon-offset value for the special rows 0x18/0xA4/0xA5.
evidence: Callers are now named (Ui_MessageWindow_BuildLines at 0x487870/0x487904) and the callees Battle_Message_SetRowAdvance/SetRowAdvanceById are named, so this is the row-offset resolver of the message layout.

name: Text_CalcRowEdgeEx
signature: s64 Text_CalcRowEdgeEx(u32 arg1, int arg2, int arg3, u32 arg4, u32 arg5)
summary: Extended row-edge calculation: blends the row's own edge with the actor box for interpolation modes 1/2 and sets the row's 'scaled' flag when the result differs.
evidence: The sole caller 0x48B558 is the named Battle_Message_ApplyRowLayout and the callee set (Text_MarkLayoutDirty, 0x48FE7C) matches the sibling row-edge helper, so the extended edge reading holds.

name: Text_CalcRowEdge
signature: u32 Text_CalcRowEdge(u32 arg1, int arg2, int arg3, u32 arg4, u32 arg5, u32 arg6, int arg7)
summary: Computes the left/right edge of a message row for the given mode (1 = actor-relative, 2 = absolute) and returns the pixel edge used by the layout, setting the row's scaled flag when needed.
evidence: Caller Battle_Message_ApplyRowLayout and the newly named Text_IsRowVisible plus the row-flag accesses match the earlier reading of the mode split (row f_9C/f_9E vs actor f_C4/f_CE).

name: Text_CalcRowLeftShift
summary: Computes the horizontal shift applied to a message row that is partly off-screen or scaled, adding a battle-RNG jitter when the shift exceeds the row's 0.0625 step; clamps the result so the row stays inside the actor box.
evidence: The old header's 'Item_LookupRecord/0x1CA3E4' hit was a misnomer: the callees are the battle RNG at work+0x5C+0x4218 (func_001CA474 is the [lo,hi] roll), so the function jitters a layout offset - it returns a value and touches no item data.

name: Text_CalcRowDamageOffset
summary: Computes the vertical offset of a damage/heal number row: interpolates from the actor box to the popup slot and adds a 0x5F..0x69 battle-RNG jitter, returning the row offset.
evidence: The RNG call at work+0x5C+0x4218 (func_001CA474, established facts) and the callers Battle_Message_ApplyRowLayout / 0x4914D4 use the result as a layout offset; it returns a value and never resolves item rows.

name: maybe_Item_GetRowMetricByCategory
summary: Returns the row metric (height) for the item equipped in slot 0 of a party member: resolves the member through 0x35EB98, reads the equipped item id with 0x6292F0, resolves the ITEM record and selects the metric for the item's category byte (+0x29) - categories 4/8/6 map to three different metrics, everything else to the default - then clamps it to the caller's value.
evidence: This is item code, not text: the body resolves a party member and the item equipped in slot 0 (0x6292F0) and goes through Item_LookupRecord, keying on the item record's +0x29 category (established facts). The old 'Ui_Text_GetTypeHeight' came from the metric table and the caller name, but the id chain is inventory. It returns a clamped value and never modifies inventory.

name: Text_CalcRowValue
signature: int Text_CalcRowValue(u32 arg1, int arg2, int arg3, u32 arg4, int arg5)
summary: Computes the value/height pair for a message row: resolves the row record (f_297) and the actor, then measures the value through the monster-UI statistic helpers.
evidence: Callers 0x4931C4/0x497690 and the now-named callees (maybe_Battle_MonsterUI_Dispatch, Text_MarkLayoutDirty, Battle_Monster_CalcHpBarFill) place it in the row layout, matching the earlier reading.

name: Battle_MonsterUI_Dispatch
signature: u32 Battle_MonsterUI_Dispatch(u32 op, BattleWork* work, int arg3, u32 ctx)
summary: Operation dispatcher for the battle monster window: op 0..N selects the HP/MP bar update, effect update, popup refresh, the vtable+0x90 hook or one of the bar/stat helpers.
evidence: The callee set is now named (Battle_Monster_CalcHpBarFill, Battle_MonsterUi_CalcStatValue, 0x492520/0x4900A8) and the nine call sites are the monster-window updates, so the dispatch role is supported.

name: maybe_Text_Row_ApplySpacingPresetC
summary: Third spacing-preset variant: tests the row-type id group beginning 0x23/0x24/0xA3, applies the spacing returned by Text_GetRowSpacing for the first present type and marks the layout dirty (default 100.0).
evidence: Text_GetRowSpacing and Text_MarkLayoutDirty are named, but the three-way 'preset' split (this one starts at 0x23/0x24/0xA3) is inferred from the id constants alone, so the C suffix and the maybe_ prefix stay.

name: Ui_BattleCommandPopup_Create
summary: Creates the small battle text popup shared by the swap and combination-command windows: allocates the widget, zeroes its fields to the 0xFF/0xFFFFF000 defaults and lazily loads the shared 'battle_Text.bxon' string table into it.
evidence: Both callers are now named (Ui_SetupSwapWindow, Ui_SetupRenkeiWindow) and the lazy table load uses the named handle helpers against the 'battle_Text.bxon' literal (0x4AAB80), so this is the shared battle-text widget, not a command popup specific to one window.

name: maybe_Ui_AnimWidget_Ctor
summary: Constructor of a small UI widget: builds the base object through 0x3259B8, installs vtable 0x77BF90 and attaches one child with 0x1A6768.
evidence: The two callers are the same Ui_SetupSwapWindow / Ui_SetupRenkeiWindow pair as 0x4AA9A4, but vtable 0x77BF90 and the child helper are unnamed, so 'animation widget' is still only a guess about what the widget displays.

name: Field_Gimmick3107_SetupDrawObjectFromDesc
signature: void Field_Gimmick3107_SetupDrawObjectFromDesc(FieldGimmick3107* self, SceneObjectDesc* desc, u32 frame)
summary: Creates the gimmick's drawable model from a passed descriptor: stores the descriptor and its two id words, copies the 0x84-byte parameter block, spawns the draw object with Field_SceneObject_CreateDrawObject and applies either the mesh or the animation depending on the descriptor kind.
evidence: The named callees (Field_SceneObject_CreateDrawObject, Field_SceneObject_SetModelSize, Gfx_SpriteActor_CreateFromTable) plus the shared prologue with 0x4B0980 describe the whole chain, matching the first pass.

name: Field_Gimmick3107_SetupDrawObjectFromTemplate
signature: void Field_Gimmick3107_SetupDrawObjectFromTemplate(FieldGimmick3107* self, SceneObjectDesc* desc, u32 frame, DrawObjectTemplate* templ)
summary: Same setup as 0x4B081C, but the model parameters (flags byte f_AC, extra word f_88, colour/scale block f_A4 and the 0x84-byte buffer) come from an already built draw object instead of a stack copy, i.e. it clones another object's appearance.

name: maybe_Field_ModelSlotEmitter_InitFromDef
signature: void maybe_Field_ModelSlotEmitter_InitFromDef(ModelSlotSet* self, int* def, u32 appearanceId, int optional)

name: maybe_Path_BuildArcLengthTable
signature: void maybe_Path_BuildArcLengthTable(void* self, u32 count, int nodeSize, int alignment, int poolId)
summary: Builds the arc-length table of a path: allocates a 0x30-byte-per-point block, evaluates the cubic curve between consecutive points (basis weights 0.125/0.25/0.5), accumulates the segment lengths into the requested table and marks the path as built.
evidence: 'Mem_AllocAlignedNodeChain' described only the allocation: the body computes cumulative lengths with cubic basis weights and is called from the now-named Path_BuildFromPoints (0x4B63D8) right after Path_ComputeDirections, which is the path builder's second half.

name: Field_ModelSlotEmitter_SpawnOne

Returns 1 when a slot was created.

name: maybe_Container_ResetListPair
summary: Resets the two embedded list heads of a container: writes each list's static vtable pointer and clears that list's owned pointers and count (via the shared release helper 0x6F5384), returning the container.

name: maybe_Field_ActorFocusSequence_Update
summary: Large state machine that focuses the view on one or two actors: toggles actor flags through the vtable, plays SE 0x28/0x33, advances a normalised 0..1 progress value, computes the world boxes of the involved actors and stores the three-float positions used to place the objects.
evidence: The body is partly destroyed by Ghidra (halt_baddata around the state dispatch) and the state constants g_004BFD6C..7C are unnamed, so although the named helpers (Game_GetWork, Field_ActorFocusSequence_MoveActor) place it in the field focus sequence, the state semantics stay uncertain.

name: Battle_RegisterActorFieldModel
summary: Registers the battle actor's field model for the current character: resolves the character id from the actor view, adds or refreshes the field party model list entry and applies the model transform through the shared field model helper.
evidence: The neighbours are named (Field_ActorFocusSequence_MoveActor, maybe_FieldParty_RegisterMemberModel, Field_FindActorEntryByModel) and the caller 0x4BF7D4 is the field/battle transition code, so the registration role holds.

name: maybe_Ui_ScreenCtor_vt7792D0

name: Text_MessageWindow_UpdateAnchors

name: Battle_Ui_PlaceMarkerOnModel
signature: u32 Battle_Ui_PlaceMarkerOnModel(BattleUnit* self, u32 arg2, u32 * out)

name: Ui_Status_CalcWeaponAttackValue
summary: Computes the displayed attack value of a party member: tests the equipped weapon's special parameter ids in priority order (0x94,0x96..0x98,0xF0..0xF2,0x99,0xBD..0xBF,0xCC), scales the parameter by the member's attack stat with 0.01 and finally adds the member's permanent bonus (f_3A4).

name: maybe_Ui_ScreenCtor_vt77C648
summary: Constructor of a UI screen class: allocates the 0x1260-byte object, installs vtable 0x77C648 and clears the four state fields at +0x498..+0x49B and the tail bytes.

name: Field_ActorEntry_Copy

name: Gfx_Movie_ShutdownTracks
summary: Tears the whole movie player down: stops every track, releases the deferred-stop event and each slot's handle and frame table, frees the slot array and marks the manager closed (0xFFFFFFFF at 0x7AE160+8).
evidence: The caller is the now-named maybe_Gfx_ResetRenderer (0x1B78F4) and the svcWaitSynchronization/svcCloseHandle pair plus the closed marker are exactly the teardown sequence, so the shutdown role holds.

name: Gfx_MovieTrack_ResetQueue

evidence: It scans the same 0x7C805C ring as the named 0x4FC8A8 path and clears the fields read by the now-named Gfx_MovieTrack_Start/Pause, so 'reset queue' is what the body does; it has no direct caller (vtable dispatch).

name: Gfx_MovieTrack_Pause
summary: Pauses a movie track by sending decoder state 2 to its handle under the player lock; out-of-range indices are ignored.
evidence: The payload 0x51A4AC(handle, 2) and the identical lock/timestamp dance as its sibling functions (0x4FC598 with state 0) make the pause/resume pair unambiguous.

name: Gfx_MovieTrack_Resume
summary: Resumes a paused movie track by sending decoder state 0 to its handle under the player lock.
evidence: Byte-identical to 0x4FC4CC except for the state argument (0 instead of 2), so the pair is pause/resume.

name: Gfx_MovieTrack_Start
summary: Starts a prepared movie track: records the track index and slot array in the slot, configures and starts the decoder channel (priority/stream id, plane pointers), then un-pauses it.
evidence: The decoder call sequence mirrors the pause/resume pair and it is the only function writing track*7 at +0x68 and the array pointer at +0x6C, so 'start' fits; it is reached through a table, hence no direct callers.

name: maybe_Sound_Voice_DetachStreams
summary: Detaches a voice from its streams: normally stops and frees every stream except the kept one and zeroes the array, otherwise only nulls the kept entry and sets the deferred flag; then it clears the voice state, unlinks it from the mixer list and calls the owner callback with reason 3.
evidence: The stop/free pair (0x51A4AC/0x519BE4) and the final block match unchanged, but the two first parameters read as (kept voice, stream array) in the signature while the body treats the second as the voice, and 0x54D4B4 (the sibling with the same flag pair) is still unnamed, so the argument roles stay uncertain.

name: Gfx_ModelResource_Release
signature: int Gfx_ModelResource_Release(GfxModelResource* self, int arg2, int arg3)

name: Gfx_ResourceSet_ApplyFormat
signature: void Gfx_ResourceSet_ApplyFormat(GfxResourceSet* self, int* record, int arg3, int kind)

name: Regex_MatchNode
summary: Recursive matcher for one regex node: handles alternation (kind 5), concatenation (0/2), groups (3/4), any-char (6/7) and match-all (8/0x12), recursing into the sub-nodes and switching between the group state's enter and leave callbacks.
evidence: The named Regex_Set_* / Regex_State_* helpers cover the character-class build and the state stack, and the kind numbers are the same grammar walk documented for the builder, so the matcher role is confirmed by the whole cluster.

name: Regex_AddCharWithFoldVariants
signature: u32 Regex_AddCharWithFoldVariants(RegexSet* set, u32 second, u32 ch)
summary: Adds a code unit plus its up-to-three case-fold variants to a character set: 0x513F78 binary-searches the 1397-entry fold table at 0x7B00EC and every non-zero alternative is inserted with the sorted interval-list insert.
evidence: The fold table contents ('I' -> 0x69/0x130/0x131, 'K' -> 0x6B/0x212A) and the now-named Regex_Set_AddRange callee make this unambiguous.

name: Regex_State_DeduplicateKeys
summary: Ensures every code unit belongs to only one class: for a key node (type 2) it removes the other key nodes with the same 16-bit key, and for every class node (type 3) containing the key it removes the key (0x513760) and frees the class when it becomes empty.
evidence: The callees are now named (Regex_State_FindOrCreate, Container_Variant_ClearChildren, Regex_Set_RemoveChar) and the type-2/type-3 split is explicit in the body, so the deduplication reading holds.

name: maybe_Regex_State_BuildRecursive
signature: u32 maybe_Regex_State_BuildRecursive(RegexMatcher* matcher, RegexState** slot, u32 key_list, u32* key)
summary: Recursive builder for a sub-expression: allocates the key bitset, marks the state's own class, deduplicates keys / splits overlapping classes, collects the child edges and recurses; finally flags each state whose key is present in the requested list.
evidence: Ghidra destroys part of the body (bad instruction data at 0x5132BE/0x5138DC, unaff_r4 as the output object), so although the surviving calls (0x5108A4, 0x51310C, 0x512E5C) are the builder steps, the recursion shape stays inferred.

name: Regex_State_CollectEdges
summary: For every class slot the bitset marks, appends all child values other than the trivial value 1 to the state's edge list, copying each value with the allocator; returns 0 on allocation failure.
evidence: The fields it reads (m[5] node array, *m+0x24 visited bits) are exactly the ones the now-named builder 0x5133C8 fills before calling it, and the copy helper 0x6E7874 is the value copier.

name: Sound_GetDisplayTime
summary: Samples the DSP display timestamp under the sound lock counter (0x5191B4/0x518BE0), computes the 64-bit delta and returns it through the caller's pair, retrying after a timeout when the DSP is not ready.

summary: Locking counterpart of 0x517E7C used by the frame update: samples the DSP timestamp and sleeps before retrying while the display is not ready; returns no timestamp.
evidence: Same caller set as 0x517E7C plus the movie playback frame path (0x4FC8A8) and the same lock/timestamp sequence minus the output pair, so it is the wait-only variant.

name: Sound_Player_StartWave
summary: Starts playing the wave described by the player: opens the CWAV, reads its wave-info block, computes the start window from the player's +0x70/+0x74 fields, allocates a note from the voice pool, copies the PCM, applies volume/pan and starts playback.
evidence: Every step is a named callee now (Sound_Cwav_Open, Sound_SeqPlayer_StartNote, Sound_Wave_Unload, 0x65EF6C) and the caller 0x550254 is the same wave-player update, so the start-wave role is confirmed.

name: Sound_WaveCache_PreloadFromFile
signature: int Sound_WaveCache_PreloadFromFile(SoundWaveCache* cache, u32 arg2, u32 fileId, SoundAllocator* alloc)
summary: Opens a small descriptor file, reads a {waveId, size} pair out of it and preloads that single wave into the cache with flag 8; used for one-wave data blocks that are not part of a group table.
evidence: The reader 0x54B5A4 and the preload call 0x54A170 plus the {id,size} pair are unchanged, and the now-named Sound_Wave_Unload neighbour confirms the wave-cache subsystem.

name: Sound_SeqPlayer_Update
summary: Main per-frame update of a sequence player: drives the async file-load state (open, wait, then decode/play), feeds the tempo step, applies the channel parameters and finally updates the playing wave.
evidence: The callees are now named (Sound_SeqPlayer_ComputeTempoStep, Sound_SeqChannel_ApplyMixParams, Sound_SeqPlayer_ReleaseChannels, Sound_Voice_SetVolumeDirect) and the state byte +0x59 mirrors the sibling 0x550254, so the frame-update role is confirmed.

name: Sound_SeqPlayer_PlayFrame
summary: Advances a playing sequence: stops and recycles the notes of all 16 channels, waits for the tempo accumulator to reach a full sample frame, then re-arms the voices and recomputes the tempo step.
evidence: The 16-channel loop and the 1/60000 tempo conversion reuse the now-named Sound_SeqChannel_Stop / Sound_SeqPlayer_ComputeTempoStep helpers, and it is called from the named update 0x555308.

name: Sound_SeqPlayer_Shutdown
summary: Destroys a sequence player: releases the channel objects, unregisters it from the driver queue, aborts the four channel-map entries and four parameter blocks, stops the pending read request and detaches from the driver registry.
evidence: It is called from the player constructor 0x555B60 and uses the named Sound_SeqPlayer_ReleaseChannels plus the registry remove helpers, which is the standard destructor sequence.

name: Sound_SeqNote_Release
summary: Fully releases a note: stops and frees its voice streams, clears the playing flags, invokes the owner completion callback with reason 0 and unlinks the note from the driver's release list.
evidence: The voice helpers are named (Sound_Voice_Stop, Sound_Voice_RecycleToPool, Sound_Voice_StopStreams) and the three callers (0x54E88C/0x54EBA4/0x54F130) are the note-lifecycle update paths, so the release role is confirmed.

name: Sound_SeqNote_Update
summary: Per-frame update of a playing note: advances the fade/priority counters, interpolates the volume/pan ramp, applies the loop and 3D parameters and, when the wave reaches its end (state 4 or the end callback), stops the streams and reports completion to the owner.
evidence: The parameter appliers are now named (Sound_Voice_RecycleToPool, Sound_Voice_Stop, Sound_Voice_StopStreams) and the 1/255 volume constant at 0.00392157 matches the note volume field, so the per-frame update reading is confirmed.

name: Sound_SeqNote_FindNoteInRange
signature: u32 Sound_SeqNote_FindNoteInRange(SoundSeqNote* note, u32 start, u32 end)
summary: Searches the sub-notes of a note for one whose [position, position+length) overlaps the requested [start, end) window and, when found, reports a range hit to the owner (callback reason 3) and clears the callback.
evidence: The 0x30-byte entry walk and the half-open interval test are unchanged, and the length comes from the now-named note-length helper 0x54C3A0; it is reached from the note/vtable code, so no direct caller.

name: maybe_Gfx_Overlay_BeginBatch
signature: void maybe_Gfx_Overlay_BeginBatch(void* state, GfxCmdBuf* cmdbuf, int* node, int* quadDesc, unsigned int limit)
summary: Resets the current command-buffer slot to its saved mark and then emits the per-screen state/texture block for an overlay quad (screen size from state->f_24, texture dimensions decoded through 0x56C738).

name: maybe_Gfx_InitTextureSlotUV

summary: Resets one of the two three-slot draw groups of a model instance: clears the three 0xCC-byte slots at +0x8C8 (group 0) or +0xB2C (group 1) and re-arms the group's counters.

name: Anim_Table_ClearActiveEntries

name: Battle2DUnit_BeginAttackSequence
summary: Prepares a unit's attack presentation for one target: reads the attack definition record, spawns a popup entry per hit and waits for the popup/effect flags before advancing the internal state.
evidence: The callees are now named (Ui_PopupEntry_SpawnForModelActors, Menu_FindSlotForEntry, Menu_OpenItemEntryWindow) and the three named Battle2DUnit_* siblings use the same state fields, so the 'begin attack sequence' slot is supported.

evidence: The chain is now all named (Monster_ModelInstance_Ctor, Ui_Screen_CtorBase, maybe_Ui_ScreenCtor_vt77B8DC, FieldParty_ResetMemberSlot, Battle_Actor_Ctor) and the vtable 0x77EAC0 is the same one used by the Battle2DUnit_* methods.

name: Battle2DUnit_BeginActionSequence
summary: Starts the next action step of a 2D battle unit: waits for one of the model motions 0x88..0x8F to finish, queues the action, refreshes the talk balloons of every sub-actor and then falls back to the shared actor state machine.

signature: void Ui_ObjectList_ReleaseAllRefPairs(UiObjectList* self, int arg2, int arg3, Heap* heap)

signature: void maybe_Ui_ObjectList_ReleaseRowHandle(UiObjectList* self, int row, int arg3, Heap* heap)

name: maybe_Ui_ObjectList_UpdateSlotOrder
signature: void maybe_Ui_ObjectList_UpdateSlotOrder(UiObjectList* self, int base, int arg3, int arg4)

name: maybe_Ui_Panel_BuildVariantEntries
signature: void maybe_Ui_Panel_BuildVariantEntries(UiPanel* self, u8* typeList, u8* end, u32 arg4)

name: Field_Gimmick_ReleaseModelHandlesA

name: Field_Gimmick_ReleaseRowModels
summary: Releases the ten row models of a field gimmick list (stride 0xC0 from +0x88) through the shared handle-release helper 0x30B5F4.

name: Gfx_HandleSlot_Destroy
summary: Destructor of a slot-handle object: releases every child through the child vtable, unlinks both intrusive lists, erases the red-black node and frees the object's slot in the global handle table (indexed by the 11-bit id at +4).
evidence: The callers are now named (Field_SceneObject_Destroy/Delete, Field_SceneObject_DtorSimple) and the global-table clear plus the rb-tree erase are the generic handle-slot teardown, so the destroy role is confirmed.

name: maybe_Field_Actor_GetMoveSpeedScale
summary: Computes an actor's movement speed multiplier and a companion flag: a style-based override for f_26A 1/2, otherwise the size class of the actor's data record (func_0063E01C, byte +0x10) selects 1.0 x {0.5, 0.6, 1.5}, which the NPC walk/run actions store as their speed.
evidence: 'GetModelScale' described the wrong use: all four callers are NPC movement initialisers (Field_NpcActionRun, Field_NpcAction_MoveToOffsetStart, Field_NpcAction_WalkToCoords_Init, maybe_Field_NpcAction_PlayScaledActionAnim) that store out[0] as their speed and use out[1] to choose the walk animation, so out[0] is a movement multiplier derived from the actor's size class.

name: Gfx_Node_SetCollisionHandle

name: Gfx_SceneSprite2D_ApplyAnimScale

name: Item_CompareNameOrderByKey
signature: bool Item_CompareNameOrderByKey(u32 arg1, const u16* idA, const u16* idB)

The decompiler warnings here are damaged input from a neighbour, not this function: the body is 210 bytes (ending at 0x71E66A) and the bad instruction sits at 0x71EFC4, far outside it, so the sort itself is intact.

name: Casino_Slot_BuildSpinResult

name: maybe_Field2D_Layer_GetField12
summary: Returns byte +0x12 of the Field2D scene's layer/config record (scene+4 -> +0x298), a small flag byte consumed by the map collision and walk-trigger code.
